markdown_content: ## Advanced Pinching Tool Overview in Clo 2025.0 This section explains the location and activation of the Advanced Pinching selection tool in Clo 2025.0, including prerequisites such as enabling simulation (CPU or GPU). It introduces the interface elements and basic usage cues like tool options visibility and selection indicators. The Advanced Pinching tool is accessible only when simulation is enabled in Clo 2025.0, either CPU or GPU mode. To activate it, first start simulation (spacebar toggle), then click and hold the selection tool icon, indicated by a small triangle for additional options, and choose "Advanced Pinching." If simulation is turned off, the advanced pinching option disappears and reappears upon reactivation. When hovering over pattern pieces or garments with this tool, two circles appear indicating selection areas: an inner circle (strong selection) and an outer circle (falloff region). These visual cues guide precise selection manipulation. --- ## Advanced Pinching Settings: Falloff Shape, Distance, and Power This section details the configurable parameters of the Advanced Pinching tool: falloff shape (bump vs. linear), falloff distance (outer circle size), and falloff power (inner circle size/intensity). It explains how these settings affect selection strength and spread. - **Falloff Shape:** Options are "Bump" or "Linear." The bump curve provides a more natural, weighted falloff effect compared to linear. The graph display changes accordingly to help visualize selection intensity distribution. - **Falloff Distance:** Controls the radius of the outer selection circle. Decreasing this value shrinks the selection area, allowing for more precise, smaller selections. Increasing it broadens the selection influence. - **Falloff Power:** Determines the size and intensity of the inner circle, which represents the core of the selection where the strongest effect occurs. Lower falloff power means a larger inner circle with less gradual falloff, resulting in a more focused selection. Higher falloff power shrinks the inner circle, increasing the transition area between strong and weak selection zones. The green overlay on the garment visualizes the strength of selection, showing which areas are fully selected versus those affected by falloff. --- ## Selection Distance Types: Surface vs. Straight This section explains the two modes for measuring selection distance in Advanced Pinching—Surface and Straight—and their impact on selection behavior. - **Surface Distance:** Measures distance along the surface topology of the pattern piece, respecting seams and garment geometry. It only selects parts connected or sewn together on the same surface. For example, a pattern edge not sewn to adjacent panels will not be selected if beyond the surface boundary, even if spatially close. - **Straight Distance:** Measures Euclidean distance in 3D space, ignoring sewing or surface boundaries. It selects all elements within a radius regardless of their attachment or surface continuity. This mode is useful when you want to move multiple pieces or layers together that are spatially near but not sewn. Examples: - A sewn seam connecting two panels will cause Surface mode to select both panels when selecting near the seam. - A detached pocket or separate layer will not be selected in Surface mode unless using Straight distance, which selects everything within the circle regardless of seams. --- ## Additional Selection Options: Distance Indicator & Limit to Selected Patterns This section describes auxiliary settings that enhance control and visualization of selections. - **Distance Indicator:** Displays the inner and outer selection circles on the garment, providing a visual reference for the selection area and falloff zones. It is recommended to keep this enabled for better precision. - **Limit to Selected Patterns:** Restricts selection and movement to only the currently selected pattern pieces. When disabled, selecting an area may affect multiple adjacent or nearby pieces depending on distance settings. This option is particularly useful for isolating edits to a single pattern piece without unintended influence on others. --- ## Practical Workflows Using Advanced Pinching This section presents practical usage scenarios demonstrating how Advanced Pinching improves garment manipulation workflows in Clo 2025.0. ### Inserting Fabric Through Small Openings A common challenge is pulling fabric through small openings or holes in garments. Previously, this required meticulous pin placement and manual adjustments. Using Advanced Pinching with simulation enabled and "Limit to Selected Patterns" active allows users to select and move fabric pieces precisely through holes with ease, significantly speeding up the process. ### Knotting and Styling Fabric Pieces Advanced Pinching enables tying knots or adjusting fabric folds by allowing users to select larger fabric regions and manipulate them smoothly. Switching between pins and advanced pinching tools gives enhanced control over fabric shaping, making it easier to create complex garment details like knots or tucks. ### Quick Styling Adjustments With the "Limit to Selected Patterns" option, users can quickly tuck parts of garments into other pieces (e.g., shirt into jeans) by selectively moving only targeted pattern pieces. This streamlines styling workflows, enabling faster and more precise garment arrangement. ### Fast Fit Corrections For garments sitting incorrectly on the avatar, Advanced Pinching facilitates rapid repositioning of large fabric areas during fitting. This reduces the need for repetitive pinning or manual adjustments, allowing users to achieve the desired fit quickly. --- ## Summary The Advanced Pinching tool in Clo 2025.0 offers refined control over pattern selection and manipulation through customizable falloff settings, intelligent distance measurement modes, and selection restrictions. It integrates seamlessly into simulation workflows to enhance garment styling, fitting, and editing efficiency. Key features include: - Activation only during simulation (CPU or GPU). - Adjustable falloff shape, distance, and power for nuanced selection influence. - Surface vs. Straight distance modes to respect garment topology or spatial proximity. - Visual distance indicators for precision. - Limit to Selected Patterns option to isolate edits. - Practical applications in fabric insertion, knot tying, styling, and fitting corrections. This tool significantly improves the user experience for designers working with complex garment simulations in Clo.
